Kuvitus: koulun laboratorion pöytä. Vase: Illustration: a school laboratory bench. On the left, a copper pendulum bob hangs on a string from a steel stand and has swung to one side; a dashed arc shows the swing. On the bench are a metre rule and a stopwatch. On the right is an open notebook whose grid shows measurement points and a straight line drawn among them. The picture has no text.
Kaavakuva kokeellisen tehtävän vaiheista: Diagram of the stages of an experimental task in two columns. On the left, planning from top to bottom: research question and hypothesis, variables and controlled quantities, instruments and repeated measurements. From the bottom an arrow leads to the right-hand column, analysis, from bottom to top: table, graph and fit, the result in the form mean x plus or minus delta x, sources of error and conclusion. From the top a dashed arrow returns to the research question: a conclusion can raise a new question.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: dekantterilasissa: Graph to scale: the mass m of cooking oil weighed in a beaker as a function of the volume V. Five measurement points at volumes of 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 cubic centimetres lie almost on a straight line. The line fitted to the points is extended as a dashed line to the vertical axis, which it cuts at b, about 52 g, not at the origin. This constant term is the mass of the beaker that was not weighed separately, that is, a systematic error. The slope k of the line is the density of the oil, about 0.91 grams per cubic centimetre, and it is shown by the triangle on the line.
Kuvaaja: heilurin jaksonajan neliö T² la: Graph: the square of the period of a pendulum T² as a function of the string length l. Six measurement points at lengths of 0.25–1.00 m lie almost on a straight line. The line fitted to the points is extended as a dashed line to the vertical axis, and it cuts the vertical axis at about 0.10 s², not at the origin. Two points of the line from which the slope is read are marked: (0.200 m; 0.91 s²) and (1.000 m; 4.12 s²). The slope is about 4.01 s²/m.
Kuvaaja: polkupyörän jarrutusmatka s nop: Graph: the braking distance s of a bicycle as a function of the square of the speed v², with the speed converted to metres per second. Five measurement points at squared speeds of 7.7–69.4 m²/s² are close to a straight line through the origin. The point (60 m²/s²; 7.2 m) is read from the line, so the slope is 0.12 s²/m.
